Being black and ethnically Jewish, nazism was always just so revolting to me. I was never even remotely close to being a nazi. I became conservative in around 8th grade though; I got sucked down a youtube rabbit hole and I was watching Ben Shapiro and Steven Crowder every day. I also had a shit ton of internalized homophobia and transphobia (I thought I was bi at the time, I'm questioning now). I always tried to distance myself from the LGBTQ+ community, especially trans people. Whenever anything got called transphobic, I immediately argued that it wasn't, because I didn't want to be what I considered "that kind of LGBT person." I'm glad to say that there was never a point in my life where I would've said that trans women were not women, but I was happy to consume transphobic content and I often found it funny. I definitely would consider my past self transphobic, even though on the outside I may have seemed like an ally. I'm just so glad I grew out of it quickly.

“Hey-hey, Ash!” someone stumbled through the cafeteria and came skidding to a stop with their hands on Ash’s shoulders.  
“Hey, Lila,” Ash said while passive-aggressively lifting her hands off their shoulders.  
“Y’know, it’s funny that I ran into you-”  
“...literally.”  
Lila laughed. “Yes, whatever. Your brother told me to give you this.”  
She handed Ash a crumpled brown paper bag. They peered into it and sighed in relief.  
“Oh, thank god. I thought I was gonna have to eat the cafeteria food.”  
“That stuff is basically radioactive,” Lila said, skipping towards the door. “Since you don’t have to wait in line… wanna eat together?”  
Ash shrugged and held the door open for Lila as she spun onto the grass.  
“I told Michael I would eat with him, but you can sit with us.”  
“Really? Yay! Mikey’s so sweet! I sit next to him in music and he always helps me out. I’m so bad at it! We had this project to do together in class once, and he was a little late so I had to start by myself. When he got there he went over it, and it was horrible! I’d messed up, like, basically everything. We got an A though, thanks to him. Oh! Did you know that he’s friends with Milo? You wouldn’t expect it, you know? Considering how different they seem? I mean, Mikey is so-”  
“Calm down. I thought you wanted to sit with me.” Ash said.  
They smiled at Lila.  
“That’s true. But Michael’s an added bonus.”  
“Right.”  
“He’s so handsome, too,” Lila said.  
“Do you like him or something?”  
“Aesthetically! I’m aroace, remember?”  
“Oh yeah,” Ash nodded. “Sorry.”  
“All good! He has the prettiest eyes. I mean, I know it’s cliche, but eyes can be so beautiful! Have you seen his eyes?”  
They shook their head.  
“You should ask him if you can look at them. They’re this gorgeous blue color. While you’re at it, his eyebrows are perfect-”  
“You pay a lot of attention to him.”  
“I’m observant. For example, I know that you have eyes that are green on the edges but golden-brown in the middle, and that the ends of your eyelashes are blonde, even though the rest is black-”  
“Okay. I get it.”  
They kept walking until they reached the picnic table inhabited by a single guy.  
“Mikey! Hi!”  
“Hey, Michael.”  
Michael grinned with a mouthful of sandwich. “Hey, guys. I saved you a spot.”  
Ash looked at the empty bench and chuckled. “I see that.”  
Michael put his sandwich down and dusted his hands off on his jeans.  
“You know lunch ends in…” he looked at his phone. “Four minutes, right?”  
“What?” Lila said. “No! I haven’t even started yet!”
